req.title: Flaskr uses sqlite as backing store
req.statement: The system shall persist users and posts in a sqlite3 database file named flaskr.sqlite by default.
triggers: flaskr uses sqlite as backing store

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the Flaskr application should use a SQLite database named 'flaskr.sqlite' to persist users and posts. The tests will verify that the application correctly interacts with this database, ensuring data persistence and correct error handling.

tests.name: test_database_persistence_positive
preconditions: The Flaskr application is initialized with a test database.
actions: Register a new user with unique credentials.
Log in with the newly registered user.
expected: The registration should succeed with a redirect to the login page.
The login should succeed with a redirect to the index page.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Register a new user
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'newuser', 'password': 'newpass'})
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

# Log in with the new user
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'newuser', 'password': 'newpass'})
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

tests.name: test_database_persistence_negative
preconditions: The Flaskr application is initialized with a test database.
actions: Attempt to register a user with an existing username.
expected: The registration should fail with an error message indicating the username is already taken.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Attempt to register with an existing username
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'newpass'})
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'User test is already registered.' in r.data

tests.name: test_database_persistence_boundary
preconditions: The Flaskr application is initialized with a test database.
actions: Attempt to register a user with a username at the boundary of allowed length.
expected: The registration should succeed if the username length is within the allowed boundary.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Register with a boundary length username
boundary_username = 'a' * 255  # Assuming 255 is the max length
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': boundary_username, 'password': 'pass'})
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
